facts_of_case: The parties are Nitu @ Priya and Gajendra, who got married in 2004. They have a daughter born out of the marriage. The husband approached the court seeking divorce on grounds of adultery and cruelty. The wife has filed an appeal against the trial court's decision.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party pleading adultery to discharge their burden.
legal_principles.held: The charge of extramarital relationship is a serious charge that causes stigma on the character of a spouse; hence, it needs to be proved by leading clinching evidence that would lead to a definite conclusion that the spouse had voluntary sexual intercourse with the person of the opposite sex other than a spouse.
cited_cases: Sangeeta Vs. Sushil, (Year) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: A handwritten note is not sufficient evidence to establish the charge of adultery.
legal_principles.held: Mere entering the house and closing the door does not constitute an illicit relationship between them, therefore, the decree of adultery cannot be granted merely based on a handwritten note.
cited_cases: Sangeeta Vs. Sushil, (Year) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: The party alleging adultery must lead clinching evidence to prove the charge.
legal_principles.held: It needs to be proved by leading clinching evidence that would lead to a definite conclusion that the spouse had voluntary sexual intercourse with the person of the opposite sex other than a spouse.
cited_cases: Sangeeta Vs. Sushil, (Year) X SCC Y

outcome.final_order: The marriage between the parties is declared dissolved.
